facts.activity_file: benching, battering and shoring an excavation

control_failures.control_label: benching, battering or shoring of an excavation
inspection and monitoring of highwalls and batters

facts.site: Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop
facts.title: positive isolation verification failure on EX-9101

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control EXCAVATION_SUPPORT: the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent, and the learning team review classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control GROUND_CONDITION_INSPECTION: the inspection and monitoring of highwalls and batters was not in place, and the learning team review classified this as an organisational factor.
Control SLOPE_MONITORING_RESPONSE: the response to slope monitoring alarms was in place but did not perform, and the learning team review classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Restore the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation on EX-9101 and record the assurance activity before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in designing and controlling excavations, specifically benching, battering and shoring an excavation. EX-9101 (earthmoving fleet) is in service for loading and dozing. The task proceeded during an intrusive maintenance task while the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent. The kinetic energy involved is held as rotating equipment, and the recorded presentation was entanglement, impact, crush.
response.summary: On 29 October 2022 an incident occurred on EX-9101 at Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop during an intrusive maintenance task, releasing kinetic energy held as rotating equipment.
